import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.formula.api import ols

# Load the dataset
invaded_niche = pd.read_csv('/data/invaded_niche_pathways.csv')

# Display the first few rows of the dataset
invaded_niche.head()

# Check for missing values
invaded_niche.isnull().sum()

# Check the data types
invaded_niche.dtypes

# Check the summary statistics
invaded_niche.describe()

# Check the correlation matrix
correlation_matrix = invaded_niche.corr()
correlation_matrix[['n.gard']].sort_values(by='n.gard', ascending=False)

# Perform a multiple linear regression to determine the factors that significantly affect the proportion of gardening-introduced non-native plants
model = ols('n.gard ~ n.unint + n.agfo + n.total + elevation + cropland.1956.50m + urban.1956.50m + cropland.1993.50m + urban.1993.50m + cropland.2009.50m + urban.2009.50m + cropland.1956.500m + urban.1956.500m + cropland.1993.500m + urban.1993.500m + cropland.2009.500m + urban.2009.500m + cropland.1956.1000m + urban.1956.1000m + cropland.1993.1000m + urban.1993.1000m + cropland.2009.1000m + urban.2009.1000m + progressive.1956.2009.50m + regressive.1956.2009.50m + no.changes.1956.2009.50m + progressive.1993.2009.50m + regressive.1993.2009.50m + no.changes.1993.2009.50m + distance.stream + distance.road + longitude + latitude + annual.temperature + annual.rainfall + annual.radiation', data=invaded_niche).fit()
anova_table = sm.stats.anova_lm(model, typ=2)
anova_table

import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm

# Load the dataset
invaded_niche = pd.read_csv('/data/invaded_niche_pathways.csv')

invaded_niche.head()

# Check for missing values
invaded_niche.isnull().sum()

# Check the data types
invaded_niche.dtypes

# Check the summary statistics
invaded_niche.describe()

# Check the correlation matrix
correlation_matrix = invaded_niche.corr()
correlation_matrix[['n.gard']].sort_values(by='n.gard', ascending=False)

# Prepare the data for regression
X = invaded_niche[['elevation', 'cropland.1956.50m', 'urban.1956.50m', 'cropland.1993.50m', 'urban.1993.50m', 'cropland.2009.50m', 'urban.2009.50m', 'progressive.1956.2009.50m', 'regressive.1956.2009.50m', 'no.changes.1956.2009.50m', 'distance.stream', 'distance.road', 'annual.temperature', 'annual.rainfall', 'annual.radiation']]
y = invaded_niche['n.gard']

# Add a constant to the model (intercept)
X = sm.add_constant(X)

# Create and fit the model
model = sm.OLS(y, X).fit()

# Display the summary of the model
model.summary()

import pandas as pd
import scipy.stats as stats
import numpy as np

# Load the dataset
invaded_niche = pd.read_csv('/data/invaded_niche_pathways.csv')

# Display the first few rows of the dataset
invaded_niche.head()

# Check for missing values
invaded_niche.isnull().sum()

# Check the data types
invaded_niche.dtypes

# Check the summary statistics
invaded_niche.describe()

# Check the correlation matrix
correlation_matrix = invaded_niche.corr()
correlation_matrix[['n.gard']].sort_values(by='n.gard', ascending=False)

# Perform a correlation analysis between 'n.gard' and other variables
correlation_results = {}
for col in invaded_niche.columns:
    if col != 'n.gard':
        corr, p_value = stats.pearsonr(invaded_niche['n.gard'], invaded_niche[col])
        correlation_results[col] = (corr, p_value)

correlation_results
